<thought>Based on the ¹H NMR, the sample shows only aromatic protons totaling five hydrogens, consistent with a monosubstituted benzene ring (C₆H₅–X) where the substituent X bears no hydrogens. This pattern matches halobenzenes such as chlorobenzene, bromobenzene, or iodobenzene. The chemical shifts (~7.5 ppm) are typical for a phenyl group attached to a halogen. The simplest candidate is chlorobenzene, whose SMILES is “c1ccccc1Cl”.</thought>
<final_answer>c1ccccc1Cl</final_answer>
